claims.statement: A Part 107 operator may request a waiver from § 107.31 by showing an equivalent level of safety; new operational-waiver applications use the Aviation Safety Hub.
claims.scope: United States Part 107 process overview; the actual waiver and current FAA application system control.
claims.reviewer: Public FAA source check; not legal advice or an approval

claims.statement: FAA states it will do its best to act on Part 107 waiver requests within 90 days, with timing varying by complexity and completeness.
claims.scope: Agency service statement, not a guaranteed processing time.
claims.reviewer: Public FAA source check; no application timing independently measured

claims.statement: FAA describes Part 91 COAs for qualifying public-aircraft operations and an expedited § 91.113 waiver path limited to entities meeting both PAO and PSO statutory definitions.
claims.scope: United States public-aircraft/public-safety overview; exact eligibility and issued conditions control.
claims.reviewer: Public FAA source check; not an eligibility determination

claims.statement: LAANC supports near-real-time requests and Part 107 further coordination above mapped values and at or below 400 feet; further-coordination requests require at least 72 hours and may be filed up to 90 days ahead.
claims.scope: United States LAANC process as published by FAA; availability and authorization conditions remain controlling.
claims.reviewer: Public FAA source check; no authorization requested

claims.statement: FAA currently routes new Part 107 operational-waiver applications through the Aviation Safety Hub while Part 107 airspace-authorization applications remain in FAADroneZone.

claims.reviewer: Public FAA source check; no application submitted
